findings.subject: Selected passages truncate supporting clauses
findings.detail: Nine compound factual claims require text outside their one submitted800-character selection. All13 have exact provenance and original-document corroboration, but onlyC3,C4,C11,C13 are fully supported by their submitted passages. findings.subject: RQ failure collection is treated as redelivery
findings.detail: Comparison2 and the contradictions paragraph treat RQ maintenance moving a job into FailedJobRegistry as redelivery/at-least-once execution. C7 and the original page establish failed-job collection, not automatic requeue/re-execution. A configured retry policy or application action must not be assumed.

findings.subject: Local deduplication does not close the external-call crash gap
findings.detail: Comparison4 presents a provider-enforced idempotency key OR a local deduplication record in the job-state transaction as protection for costly requests. A local transaction cannot atomically cover an external effect: a crash after remote success but before local outcome persistence remains ambiguous. Recommendation5 correctly conditions its provider-key advice on provider support, but does not make the comparison equivalent/safe. Ambiguous calls need reconciliation/no blind retry, not an exactly-once claim.

findings.subject: Recommendation premises and fencing remain incompletely established
findings.detail: SQLite simplicity is a plausible explicitly labelled inference for this scope. The only-no-separate-server comparison and the concrete IMMEDIATE/lease queue recipe are not established byC1-C4. The broker recommendation overstates supervision out of the box, despite recommending external managers. Temporal timers/signals/child-workflow and deployment-cost premises are not supported byC10/C11 selected evidence. Lease expiry alone is not stale-worker fencing; the report acknowledges gaps but does not supply the requested precise comparison.
